clue.text: Take the consequences of buying concert ticket?

definitions.meaning: to accept the unpleasant results of one's own actions, an idiom
read literally, paying to go and sit in front of an orchestra and its performance

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether paying for a concert seat means accepting the fallout.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: buying a ticket lets you literally sit facing the performers and their sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means accepting punishment or blame; the joke reading is sitting opposite the orchestra.

clue.text: Continent that includes Sweden, your old country

indicators.note: the continent includes, so holds inside it, the next pieces

parts.note: Asia is a continent
S is the international vehicle code for Sweden
YR is a written abbreviation for your

explanation.surface: Someone describes their former homeland as part of a continent containing Sweden.
explanation.walkthrough: Assyria was an ancient empire in Mesopotamia.
explanation.definitionFit: Assyria was an ancient kingdom of the Middle East, a nation long gone.

clue.text: No longer a case for full exercise of rights

parts.note: ex means former, no longer so
an action is a case at law, a lawsuit

explanation.surface: Something was once a legal argument for exercising rights fully.
explanation.definitionFit: An exaction is the strict demanding or enforcing of a payment or due.

clue.text: Accesses internet site for popular records

definitions.meaning: visits to a web page are counted as page views

explanation.surface: A site is visited for its chart-topping records.
explanation.definitionFit: Website visits are counted as hits, and smash records are also hits.

clue.text: Thirteenth-century rights issue?

parts.note: a share issue in finance is suggested, but the rights are constitutional ones granted by King John in 1215

explanation.surface: A medieval sale of shares to existing stockholders.
explanation.walkthrough: A rights issue is a stock offer to existing shareholders, apt for the Financial Times; here the 'rights' are the liberties the charter of 1215 set out.
explanation.definitionFit: The great charter of 1215 set down English liberties, a famous document granting rights.

clue.text: Pulls up beautiful lawn

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: draws means pulls, as a horse draws a cart

explanation.surface: Someone tears up a lovely lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Sward is a literary word for an expanse of grassy turf.

clue.text: In prevailing weather, I may go with friend after class

indicators.note: after sends the letter and friend behind the class abbreviation, which comes first

parts.note: CL is the written abbreviation for class
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: A pupil hopes to walk out with a pal after a lesson, whatever the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Climate is the usual pattern of conditions in a region over time.

clue.text: After advance payment, one getting less for firm engaged on project?

indicators.note: after puts the second piece behind the first

parts.note: a sub is an advance on wages
something contracting is getting smaller, so it is a contractor

explanation.surface: A worker paid in advance ends up earning less from the firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link; 'one getting less' is the whimsical sense of a thing that contracts.
explanation.definitionFit: A subcontractor is a company taken on by the main contractor to do part of a job.

clue.text: Convicts over counterfeit children's game

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: convicts are prisoners
base means debased or fake, as in base coin

explanation.surface: Inmates are caught passing fake money.
explanation.walkthrough: Prisoner's base is an old chasing game in which captured players are held at a base.
explanation.definitionFit: Prisoners' base is a traditional playground chasing game.

clue.text: New arrival out of bed before dawn

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the second in the answer

parts.note: someone out of bed is up
the dawn of something is its start or beginning

explanation.surface: A newborn, or a new arrival at a house, is awake before daybreak.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is a newcomer who has risen suddenly, often presumptuously, to importance.

clue.text: Good to give lead to more idle workman

indicators.note: the first piece leads, so it is placed at the front of the second

parts.note: lazier means more idle

explanation.surface: A good example is supposedly set to motivate a lazier labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: A glazier is a tradesman who fits glass into windows, a kind of skilled worker.

clue.text: He painted waterbird around river

indicators.note: the bird's name goes around the river's letter, so the abbreviation sits inside it

parts.note: a coot is a black water bird

explanation.surface: An artist made a picture of a bird near a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: Jean-Baptiste-Camille Corot was a 19th-century French landscape painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Corot was a French landscape artist, so he is the man who painted.

clue.text: Secure service in Australia, for example

parts.note: to land something is to secure or win it
Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: Someone tries to get a church service held down under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link; 'Australia' looks like part of the scene but is the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia is a continent, a large expanse of territory; an example of a large continuous body of land.

clue.text: Proper view of characteristic of Perpendicular?

parts.note: right means proper or correct
an angle is a viewpoint or point of view

explanation.surface: An architectural historian gives the correct take on the Perpendicular style.
explanation.walkthrough: Perpendicular is the late English Gothic architectural style, but here it just means at ninety degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines that are perpendicular meet at ninety degrees, so this is their defining feature.

clue.text: Italian on Palatine, having a tour

indicators.note: the letters go on a tour, wandering about into a new order

explanation.surface: An Italian walks around the Palatine Hill in Rome as a sightseer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having a tour' rearranges ON PALATINE; the Palatine is one of Rome's seven hills.
explanation.definitionFit: A Neapolitan is a native of Naples, so an Italian person.

clue.text: Judge returned to nuclear plant

indicators.note: returned means the word for the judge is read backwards

parts.note: a ref, short for referee, is a judge in sport

explanation.surface: A judge has gone back to work at a nuclear power station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like an industrial site but is a green plant. The printed TERN is an OCR slip: the wordplay builds FERN.
explanation.definitionFit: A fern is a flowerless green plant with feathery fronds.

clue.text: Guerrilla I found in separate hospital

indicators.note: the letter is found inside, so it is placed within the other pieces

parts.note: to part is to separate
san is short for sanatorium, a hospital

explanation.surface: A rebel fighter is discovered in an isolation ward.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan is a member of an irregular armed resistance force.

clue.text: Banter from the bar

definitions.meaning: to jest or scoff at someone, a sort of mocking talk
a ... is a horizontal bar, as in a towel ...

explanation.surface: Joking talk overheard in the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Railing is mocking or scolding talk, and a rail is a straight bar.

clue.text: In position, say, showing awareness

indicators.note: say means the words are spoken, giving a word that is pronounced the same

parts.note: in position means in site, on the spot

explanation.surface: Being on the spot proves one is alert.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is understanding or perception; showing awareness is exercising it.

clue.text: One from up north sent her lad off

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: A mother sent her boy away northwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SENT HER LAD. The Shetland Islands lie far to the north of mainland Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A Shetlander is a native of the Shetland Islands, the northernmost part of Britain.

clue.text: Cause confusion with a gender change

indicators.note: change tells you to alter the order of the letters

explanation.surface: Switching gender causes confusion.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange is to throw into disorder or disturb.

clue.text: Robinson Crusoe — why it's not being performed?

definitions.meaning: Defoe's hero is shipwrecked alone on an island
a play goes unperformed because its actors, the cast, are elsewhere

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a production of Robinson Crusoe has been cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Crusoe is a shipwrecked man stranded on an island; the joke is a play's actors being absent.

clue.text: Morning's cold — get old cloak

parts.note: AM stands for ante meridiem, the morning
ice is extremely cold

explanation.surface: A chilly morning calls for an old coat.
explanation.walkthrough: An amice is a cloak or hood worn by clergy in the Middle Ages.
explanation.definitionFit: An amice is a medieval ecclesiastical hooded cape, a garment from the past.

clue.text: Beat time, having realised orchestra blindly follow their leaders

indicators.note: follow puts the picked letters after the first piece
the leaders of those four words are their first letters, taken in order

explanation.surface: A conductor marks time while the players obediently follow without thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a strong rhythmic pulse, a beat.

clue.text: I almost stand for flag

indicators.note: almost means stopping short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to rise is to stand up

explanation.surface: Someone nearly stands to salute a banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' looks like a banner, but it is the plant: the yellow flag is a wild iris.
explanation.definitionFit: Flag is the common name for wild irises, such as the yellow flag.

clue.text: Still effective at moment of departure

definitions.meaning: read as two words, ..., at the point of leaving

explanation.surface: Something remains valid right up until someone leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Ongoing means continuing; split as two words it means at the point of leaving.

clue.text: Feels badly about gifts not being opened

indicators.note: a thing not opened has lost its front, so the first letter goes

parts.note: presents are gifts

explanation.surface: Someone is upset that their presents are still wrapped.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to feel bitter or aggrieved about it.

clue.text: The very best caps for busy workers

definitions.meaning: an idiom for the finest, the most excellent
kneecaps belonging to busy insects, the honey-makers proverbially hard at work

explanation.surface: Ideal hats for people who work hard.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means something outstanding; literally, the kneecaps of the industrious insects.
